item.title: Get Started with MySQL - VS Code
item.description: This comprehensive guide is tailored to help you kickstart your journey with MySQL, especially if you’re new to the platform. We’ll delve into the essentials, from an insightful introduction to databases and an exploration of MySQL as a Relational Database Management System (RDBMS) to the installation of MySQL Server, establishing connections, and navigating through a sample database. Introduction to MySQL MySQL stands out as a popular open-source relational database management system, providing efficient tools for organizing and retrieving data.

item.title: Introduction to MySQL
item.description: MySQL is a widely used relational database management system (RDBMS) that is used to store and manage data for a variety of applications. It is an open-source software that is developed and maintained by Oracle Corporation. MySQL is one of the most popular RDBMS solutions in the world, and it is used by millions of developers and organizations. In this blog post, we will explore what MySQL is, how it works, and why it is such an important tool for developers and businesses.

item.title: Install MySQL Server
item.description: Install MySQL Server on Windows In this tutorial, you’ll discover the step-by-step process of installing MySQL Server and its related products on a Windows operating system using the MySQL Installer. By the end of the tutorial, you’ll have a MySQL Server or XAMPP Control Panel (You can either Install MySQL Server or Xampp, One of the choose is compulsory ) and its tools installed on your system, ready for learning and practice.

item.title: Connect to MySQL - VS Code
item.description: If you choose to install MySQL Server instead of XAMPP while following the step-by-step guide on Install MySQL , you will be able to use the command-line client of MySQL. If you choose XAMPP Control Panel, then you can access the MySQL server from phpMyAdmin by starting both Apache and MySQL servers from the XAMPP Control Panel. Connect to MySQL Using mysql Command-line Client The mysql command-line client is a powerful tool that allows you to interact with MySQL in interactive and non-interactive modes.

item.title: Employees_db Sample Database
item.description: MySQL Sample Database We leverage the classicmodels database as a MySQL sample database to accelerate your MySQL learning journey. The classicmodels database portrays a retailer specializing in scale models of classic cars. It encompasses typical business data, including customer information, product details, sales orders, sales order line items, and more. In our MySQL tutorials, we utilize this sample database to illustrate a diverse range of MySQL features, from basic queries to intricate stored procedures.

item.title: MySQL SELECT FROM
item.description: In this tutorial, you will learn how to use the basic form of the MySQL SELECT FROM statement to query data from a table. Introduction to MySQL SELECT FROM statement The SELECT statement allows you to select data from one or more tables. To write a SELECT statement in MySQL, you use this syntax: SELECT select_list FROM table_name; In this syntax: First, specify one or more columns from which you want to select data after the SELECT keyword.
